# Shared still/film authoring fixture

[Fixture overview](../../README.md) · [Primary test](../../../example-poster-and-film.e2e.ts)
· [Workbench tests](../../../workbench.e2e.ts)
· [Workbench resource tests](../../../workbench-resources.e2e.ts)

## Coverage

Exercises shared image/font Assets in one Project with independent still targets
and a short film. Tests use actual browser font loading, image capture, workbench
saves, stale-state detection, Take reuse and portable export. Workbench tests also
reuse the bundled CJK font for resource resolution.

## Inputs and targets

| Input | Test role |
| --- | --- |
| `poster.html` / `poster.css` | Editable 1200×1500 document shared by `print` and `print-2x` |
| `social.html` / `social.css` | Independent 1080×1080 document and `social` target |
| `film.html` / `film.mjs` | Silent 640×360, 24 fps picture Source |
| `assets/light.png` | Deterministic 1200×800 PNG generated by the recipe |
| `fonts/` | Real CJK/Latin font inputs and their complete OFL texts |
| [create.mjs](create.mjs) | Declares documents, three still targets, film, Assets and handoffs |

`print-2x` is 2400×3000. Recipe `frames` is an integer >= 8, default 48.
The still documents have no independent timeline; the composition belongs to the
film. The fixture's film is silent so image/film lifecycle assertions do not
depend on a soundtrack.

## Maintenance

- Keep two targets on the poster document and another on the social document.
  This distinguishes shared-document invalidation from independent-target reuse.
- Keep film inputs shared at the Asset level without importing `poster.html`.
  A poster edit must stale its stills while reusing the unchanged film Take;
  changing the shared PNG must also invalidate the film's picture input.
- Keep real font files and overlapping text/image geometry. Tests check font
  readiness and occlusion rather than accepting an image with fallback glyphs.
- Workbench saves must update author bytes and reject stale edits. Exported
  copies must render after the original directory is unavailable.
- Delivery selectors determine product files, while the full editable Project
  travels with each handoff. Keep selector and missing/stale-target checks
  separate from rendering; delivery itself must not produce missing images.
- Preserve `create.mjs` font rights, original subset bytes and full licence
  handoffs. Source/Asset hashes are computed by the authoring API.

## The test fonts

The four WOFF2 files and two OFL texts in `fonts/` are fixture bytes, not a
product font library. They are the same real subsets the poster/film regression
was written against:

| File | Family | Weight | Upstream source | Bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NotoSansSC-400-subset.woff2` | Noto Sans SC | 400 | `@fontsource/noto-sans-sc@5.2.8` → `noto-sans-sc-chinese-simplified-400-normal.woff2` | 546692 |
| `NotoSansSC-700-subset.woff2` | Noto Sans SC | 700 | `@fontsource/noto-sans-sc@5.2.8` → `noto-sans-sc-chinese-simplified-700-normal.woff2` | 561368 |
| `SpaceGrotesk-400-subset.woff2` | Space Grotesk | 400 | `@fontsource/space-grotesk@5.2.8` → `space-grotesk-latin-400-normal.woff2` | 13456 |
| `SpaceGrotesk-700-subset.woff2` | Space Grotesk | 700 | `@fontsource/space-grotesk@5.2.8` → `space-grotesk-latin-700-normal.woff2` | 12780 |

Both families are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; the verbatim texts are
`OFL-NotoSansSC.txt` and `OFL-SpaceGrotesk.txt` beside them. Neither declares a
Reserved Font Name, so the subsets keep the upstream names. The Latin files are
fontsource's `latin` range. The two Noto files are cut from the
`chinese-simplified` range with `pyftsubset` over GB2312 level 1 (3751 hanzi) plus
ASCII, Latin-1, general punctuation, CJK punctuation and full-width forms; that
covers ordinary Chinese copy and this fixture's lines, **not** the full CJK block.
A design that needs a rarer character must regenerate the subset with that
character instead of assuming coverage.
